questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road.
No parking.
Right lane closed.
Multiple turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves. You should slow down.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to get through before it turns red.
Keep driving. You have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Look at what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass going downhill than smaller vehicles.
Turn in a smaller space than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass going uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are large and heavy, they need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles do.

questions.question: Distracted drivers have higher crash risk when using which of these?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player while driving is dangerous. Even hands-free phones can distract you. These distractions increase your crash risk.

questions.question: What provides the best protection in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash and greatly reduce serious injury. Airbags work best with safety belts to protect you in front-end crashes. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and roll down your window.
Have your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel. Wait for the officer to approach.
Get out and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel. Wait for the officer to approach.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and ask passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your vehicle unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance card.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of an accident.
It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stress and strong emotions hurt your driving ability. If you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress reduces your focus on the road. It is better to wait to drive until you feel calm.

questions.question: When merging onto an expressway behind other vehicles, what is most important?

options.text: Watch the vehicle behind you.
Adjust your speed and position to match traffic flow.
Stay very close to the vehicle in front of you.
Turn off your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your speed and position to match traffic flow.
questions.explanation: Merge smoothly by matching the speed and flow of traffic. Trucks may not be able to move for you. It is safest to blend in with traffic as smoothly as possible.

questions.question: Why is city driving more dangerous than expressway driving?

options.text: Lower speed limits.
Narrower driving lanes.
Cross traffic and pedestrians.
Worse road conditions in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Intersection crashes cause more deaths and serious injuries than crashes on any other road. Watch for vehicles and pedestrians at all times. Some may ignore traffic signals or signs.

questions.question: What should you do at a school crossing sign?

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross first. Be alert for pedestrians when driving through intersections or turning. Yield to anyone in or entering a crosswalk.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what happens?

options.text: It slows down your reactions.
It makes you feel more confident.
It breaks down faster in your body.
It reduces driving mistakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: It slows down your reactions.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident, and causes you to make more mistakes.

questions.question: What does an octagonal sign always mean?

options.text: Speed limit sign
Stop sign
Hospital sign
Railroad warning sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign
questions.explanation: Octagonal signs are always stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
An intersection is coming up.
Road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane on a multilane road ends ahead. Traffic in the right lane must move left.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle while driving?

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign
When a red light is on
When a traffic officer orders you to stop
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: On a freeway, you missed your exit. What should you do?

options.text: Make a quick turn from your lane.
Stop and back up.
Continue until you reach the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue until you reach the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not back up. Go to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a shoulder or freeway is illegal.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or lights. What should you do?

options.text: Approach with caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn your radio down to listen for a train.
Only continue if a flagger signals you to go.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Lower your radio volume to listen for trains. Obey all flagger instructions.

questions.question: An officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light. What should drivers do?

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: When a traffic officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic light signals.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention while driving
Driving too fast for conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Driving too fast is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Do not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with it.
Ignore any defects so you do not embarrass your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn how the vehicle's equipment works before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn how the vehicle's equipment works before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take a few minutes to find and learn how to use the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving?

options.text: It slows reflexes and reaction time.
It puts you to sleep.
It wakes you up.
It improves your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It slows reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows brain activity and reduces the skills you need for safe driving. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted across traffic lanes?

options.text: On curves and hills.
Next to churches and schools.
At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
On freeway on-ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This chevron sign warns that the road curves sharply in the direction shown by the arrow. Multiple signs may appear along the curve.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights approaches?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination before it catches up.
Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must yield to all emergency vehicles with sirens or flashing lights. Pull to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car ahead slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
You may not see the vehicle's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car ahead slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: Following too closely means you won't have enough time to stop if the car in front of you stops or slows down suddenly. This can cause a collision.

questions.question: What should you do when passing other vehicles?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane only when you can see the front of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is starting.
A steep hill is ahead.
The overpass ahead has low clearance.
Two lanes of opposite traffic are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overpass is low. Do not go under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Loosely.
Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Hidden beneath the seat.
So that the seat belt buzzer or light does not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should sit comfortably so you can fit your fist between it and your chest.

questions.question: What helps a person overcome the effects of alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime.
Hot coffee.
Fresh air.
Only time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time.
questions.explanation: Only time allows the body to overcome the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: If a train is close enough or fast enough to be dangerous, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait until the train has completely passed before crossing the tracks.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find an alternative route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the train has completely passed before crossing the tracks.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is near or moving fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are broken.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Sit in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on a highway, turn on your hazard flashers. Exit the road safely and park where other drivers can see you. Raise your hood to show your vehicle is disabled.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, what should you do?

options.text: You cannot exit the freeway.
You can continue through or exit from your current lane.
You can stay in your lane and continue through.
You must exit if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must exit if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means your lane will exit the freeway. You have two choices: change lanes to continue through, or stay in your lane and exit the freeway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Emergency vehicles are ahead.
An uncontrolled intersection is ahead.
A four-way stop is ahead.
A traffic signal is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic signal is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When you are going through an intersection.
When you are passing a bicyclist.
When you see a child about to run into the street.
When you are parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others who may not see you. For example, honk if a child is about to run into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Keep a larger distance between you and other cars.
Do not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Take these steps to stay safe and protect other drivers on the road.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt?

options.text: The driver.
A front seat passenger.
Any child under age 16.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: The driver, front seat passengers, and all children under age 16 must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle. Police can stop your vehicle if anyone is not buckled up.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, what should you use to show you are turning?

options.text: Your horn.
Your headlights.
Hand signals.
Your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals.
questions.explanation: When your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers you are changing direction.

questions.question: You are angry after something happens at work. When you get to your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play the radio loud so you do not think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to feel better.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home.
Stop at a bar for a few drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home.
questions.explanation: If you are angry or upset, wait before you drive. Driving while emotional is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: What do orange signs mean?

options.text: Work zone signs.
Rule signs.
School zone signs.
Direction signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn you about work zones on the highway. These diamond-shaped signs have black letters and tell you that workers are nearby.

questions.question: What can make it harder for someone to drive safely?

options.text: Alcohol.
Medication.
Not getting enough sleep.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires being in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and being tired can all make driving unsafe.

questions.question: How can you prevent getting tired on a long drive?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: On long trips, stop every two hours for a break. If you feel sleepy, pull over and nap or find a place to stay for the night.

questions.question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?

options.text: Slow down at the light.
Drive carefully without stopping.
Merge to the right.
Stop before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Yield to all traffic and pedestrians. Only go when it is safe. At railroad crossings, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices are off before crossing.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give motorcycles the full width of one lane. Even if there seems to be room to share the lane, motorcycles need space to move safely.

questions.question: On long trips, how can you prevent drowsiness?

options.text: Turn on your car radio.
Slow down.
Stop at regular intervals to rest.
Move your eyes from side to side as you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at regular intervals to rest.
questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, stop regularly to rest. Take time to stretch, even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. Always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass if an oncoming vehicle is in the passing lane, if your view is blocked by a curve or hill, at an intersection, before or on a railroad crossing or bridge, or in a no passing zone. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: What causes "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep the night before.
Driving short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: "Highway hypnosis" happens when you stare straight ahead at the road and stop looking ahead, behind, and around. You may zone out and crash into traffic that is slowing or stopping.

questions.question: What does a good defensive driver do?

options.text: Drives slowly at all times.
Watches for the actions of other drivers.
Travels at a constant speed.
Only drives in familiar areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches for the actions of other drivers.
questions.explanation: Even experienced drivers can become distracted. A defensive driver watches for what other drivers do and expects problems before they happen.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrives first.
The driver who arrives last.
One driver should continue without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, all traffic must stop. The first vehicle to reach the intersection goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What is true about traffic signs and pavement markings?

options.text: They must always be obeyed.
They are just suggestions.
They must be followed only when other traffic is present.
They must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must always be obeyed.
questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and inform drivers of road conditions. They help guide you safely to your destination. You must always obey them.

questions.question: When it begins to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than surrounding traffic.
Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive closely behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When heavy rain reduces visibility, slow down. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is too heavy to see clearly, pull onto the shoulder and stop until it clears.
